#### 5.11.11. Physical hardware campaign design and release risk
**Frame/thermal stress risk:** misleading sound analogy, ring overdraw and strobe risk. Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `interference clouds form luminous 3D harmonic knots; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND6_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round6/chord-chamber/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D2:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND6_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round6/chord-chamber/D2.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad Pro M5, iPadOS 27.2 large-device layout passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
- **D3:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND6_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round6/chord-chamber/D3.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPad A16, iPadOS 26.5 compatibility and slow tier passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.
**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 12. Polyhedron Courier — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G12`)
**Source:** `G429`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.37 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Guide a bead over faces of a rotating polyhedron by unfolding pathways. **Signature animated environment:** articulated solids and vivid edge-trail highlights; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. **Core abstraction:** hinged face net.
#### 5.12.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees articulated solids and vivid edge-trail highlights; reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Guide a bead over faces of a rotating polyhedron by unfolding pathways. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `hinged face net` computational rules, visual `articulated solids and vivid edge-trail highlights; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials` and player control arrangement `Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.12.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** R_i(θ_i) transforms adjacent faces around shared edge; reject 3D triangle intersections. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Guide a bead over faces of a rotating polyhedron by unfolding pathways. Normalize input into `PolyhedronCourierAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** fold a legal geometric net into a connected target solid without self-collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over discretized hinge states with swept triangle intersection. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** folding singularities, Z-fighting, hidden face gestures. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.12.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting articulated solids and vivid edge-trail highlights; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable hinged face net handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with guide a bead over faces of a rotating polyhedron by unfolding pathways; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative hinged face net predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.12.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted polyhedron mesh, glowing seams and easing hinge transforms. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** articulated solids and vivid edge-trail highlights; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `PolyhedronCourierScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `PolyhedronCourierParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `77af0f28e5ae` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.12.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 13. Origami Orbit — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G13`)
**Source:** `G432`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.37 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Fold thin solar sails to capture light and change a miniature orbit. **Signature animated environment:** folding polygon sails glint around a tiny planetoid; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. **Core abstraction:** hinged face net.
#### 5.13.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees folding polygon sails glint around a tiny planetoid; reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Fold thin solar sails to capture light and change a miniature orbit. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `hinged face net` computational rules, visual `folding polygon sails glint around a tiny planetoid; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials` and player control arrangement `Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.13.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** R_i(θ_i) transforms adjacent faces around shared edge; reject 3D triangle intersections. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Fold thin solar sails to capture light and change a miniature orbit. Normalize input into `OrigamiOrbitAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** fold a legal geometric net into a connected target solid without self-collision. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** graph search over discretized hinge states with swept triangle intersection. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** folding singularities, Z-fighting, hidden face gestures. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.13.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting folding polygon sails glint around a tiny planetoid; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable hinged face net handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with fold thin solar sails to capture light and change a miniature orbit; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative hinged face net predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold and rotate a 3D net to complete a connectivity puzzle. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.13.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** faceted polyhedron mesh, glowing seams and easing hinge transforms. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** folding polygon sails glint around a tiny planetoid; Reconfigurable polyhedral nets, articulated hinges, procedural faceted materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `OrigamiOrbitScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `OrigamiOrbitParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `c8623a98a1f5` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.13.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct hinged face net controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.

Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.

### 14. Dustlight Labyrinth — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G14`)
**Source:** `G391`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.36 /100**, proposed upfront price **$2.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Illuminate particle streams only at correct points to infer invisible exits. **Signature animated environment:** smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes. **Core abstraction:** bounded field integrator.
#### 5.14.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Illuminate particle streams only at correct points to infer invisible exits. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `bounded field integrator` computational rules, visual `smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes` and player control arrangement `Shepherd particle clusters through spatial constraints`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.14.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** v+=a(x,t)Δt; x+=vΔt, fixed step; stable particle IDs and bounded occupancy. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Illuminate particle streams only at correct points to infer invisible exits. Normalize input into `DustlightLabyrinthAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** steer clusters into target regions while avoiding forbidden regions. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** sampled state-space field-controller search and cluster membership proof. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** particle overdraw, thermals on D3, non-deterministic GPU sorting. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.14.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable bounded field integrator handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with illuminate particle streams only at correct points to infer invisible exits; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative bounded field integrator predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Shepherd particle clusters through spatial constraints. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.14.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** GL_POINT sprites, instanced halos, fade trails and glow compositing. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `DustlightLabyrinthScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `DustlightLabyrinthParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `fd6dd972a21a` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.14.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct bounded field integrator controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

#### 5.14.10. Cross-model render, endurance, abnormal state and deterministic fault-injection matrix
| Case | Initial condition | Mutation | Expected invariant / visual evidence |

Run repeated renderer-bound iterations of `smoky glitter streams outline unseen maze edges; Batched additive point sprites, deterministic field integration and trail meshes` at bounded maximum procedural complexity for 30 minutes on D3; measure actual frame pacing via CADisplayLink, memory/thermal history, cold and warm scene load. Device observations cannot be prefilled in the document.
- **D1:** use a signed automation-only Release-like build with `ROUND6_AUTOMATION`, install with `devicectl`, execute win/reject/replay and endurance mode, export `Documents/round6/dustlight-labyrinth/D1.json`, inspect screenshot and actual output, run on-device XCTest if supported, hash bundles/results. Record actual model/build/UDID and timing; never claim iPhone 15, iOS 27.0.1 baseline, narrow-screen touch passed unless evidence exists. Auto-Lock/trust/signing may block owner-only and must be reported.

**Release policy:** premium one-time price, no ads, ad SDKs, IAP, subscriptions, external image assets or account dependence. Performance, stability, commercial desirability and trademark name clearance remain empirical/procedural decision gates. If this game turns out too similar to another app, redesign or combine; do not publish reskins.

### 15. Rotary Stairwell — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G15`)
**Source:** `G315`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.35 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Twist stacked tower floors to create a continuous helix to the summit. **Signature animated environment:** spiral stair geometry glows within translucent walls; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. **Core abstraction:** room hinge graph.
#### 5.15.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees spiral stair geometry glows within translucent walls; hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Twist stacked tower floors to create a continuous helix to the summit. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `room hinge graph` computational rules, visual `spiral stair geometry glows within translucent walls; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows` and player control arrangement `Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.15.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** world transforms of connected panels rotate around shared manifold hinges. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Twist stacked tower floors to create a continuous helix to the summit. Normalize input into `RotaryStairwellAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** create a continuous navigable route after rotating and folding room sections. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** hinge-state graph search plus reachability and collision certificates. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** unintended paths through seams, camera clipping, deceptive geometry. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.15.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting spiral stair geometry glows within translucent walls; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable room hinge graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with twist stacked tower floors to create a continuous helix to the summit; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative room hinge graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Fold room panels so a navigable route or optical pattern completes. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.15.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** procedural architectural panel meshes, normal-mapped-in-code faceting. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** spiral stair geometry glows within translucent walls; Hinged procedural meshes, solid-to-net transforms, planar projection shadows. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `RotaryStairwellScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `RotaryStairwellParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `ab2cec321299` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.15.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.

- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct room hinge graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

### 16. Chromatic Observatory — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G16`)
**Source:** `G206`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.35 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations. **Signature animated environment:** spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. **Core abstraction:** ray/wave optical graph.
#### 5.16.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, sdf optics and gradient materials, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `ray/wave optical graph` computational rules, visual `spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials` and player control arrangement `Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.16.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations. Normalize input into `ChromaticObservatoryAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** route or phase-align rays through specified optical stations. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 7 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** bounded ray graph traversal with plane intersections and reflection/refraction validation. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** false physical accuracy, firefly pixels, excessive transparency. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.16.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable ray/wave optical graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative ray/wave optical graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Tap and rotate optical elements; observe ray path; solve light-path constraint. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.16.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** projected caustics, beam cylinders, chromatic dispersion approximations. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `ChromaticObservatoryScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `ChromaticObservatoryParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `583dae20cf4a` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.16.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct ray/wave optical graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.

#### 5.16.7. Full feature-by-feature Spec Kit workflow; every invocation has its own complete prompt
##### R06-G16-01: Domain rules & normalized action contract
**Scope:** Implement exact game state, action sanitization, illegal move failures and win predicates; no renderer-owned truth. **Inputs and decisions:** Align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations. **Physics contract:** Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. **Renderer identity:** spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. **Pass gate:** solver witnesses, test commands and intended source files are inspectable.
**/speckit-specify** — invoke the installed Claude Desktop skill with this FULL prompt:
```text
/speckit-specify — feature R06-G16-01 — Domain rules & normalized action contract.
TARGET: Chromatic Observatory; source scope Wave optics; active Spec Kit feature directory: specs/r06-g16-01-domain-rules-normalized-action-cont/. Prior scope: VisualCore root CLAUDE.md, README.md, round2.md and all earlier completed rounds, current round6.md. Consumers: Chromatic Observatory.
PRODUCT INTENT: Align observatory shutters to separate three overlapping constellations. HERO ART: spectral light cones and shimmering architectural lenses; Analytic beam volumes, layered caustic projections, SDF optics and gradient materials. Feature contract: Implement exact game state, action sanitization, illegal move failures and win predicates; no renderer-owned truth. Existing math foundation: Snell n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2; Fresnel-inspired aesthetic only, numeric ray solver owns truth. Solver/proof basis: bounded ray graph traversal with plane intersections and reflection/refraction validation.
IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARIES: use already built VisualCore public adapters and existing EGL/OpenGL ES/ANGLE Metal backend. ### 17. Vibration Garden — complete proposed implementation design (`R06-G17`)
```
**Source:** `G228`, source `Newly proposed 300; assessed from analog family prior`, conceptual score **93.35 /100**, proposed upfront price **$3.99**. *This is a design decision, not actual sales or in-engine measured quality.*
**One-sentence pitch:** Tune ground resonators to make dormant geometric plants unfold. **Signature animated environment:** radial substrate ripples trigger recursive metallic blooms; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals. **Core abstraction:** pulse propagation graph.
#### 5.17.1. Product identity, audience, differentiation and non-goals
The player sees radial substrate ripples trigger recursive metallic blooms; instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals, then learns that every luminous element represents an actual state variable of a puzzle built around the following verb: Tune ground resonators to make dormant geometric plants unfold. The premium promise is one decisive, tactile 3D interaction, one clear target, satisfying action feedback and a complete offline catalog. No artificial wait timers, no ad gating, no login, no in-app purchases. The programmatic graphics are the product: the game must be more understandable **because** the particles, shadows, waves or solids move. Use SwiftUI only for menus and accessibility; real scene objects are driven by reusable VisualCore GLES/ANGLE draw paths.
This title must be uniquely distinguishable from other games by its `pulse propagation graph` computational rules, visual `radial substrate ripples trigger recursive metallic blooms; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals` and player control arrangement `Position/trigger resonators and infer hidden 3D structure`. Create a side-by-side gameplay-differentiation table against all previously released VisualCore apps and the other 24 current concepts. Reject it if the input and goals could be reused unchanged by reskinning another application.
#### 5.17.2. Explicit mathematical state and success/failure rules
- **State model:** arrival_time(x)=||x-source||/c with bounded distance field and quantized pulse ticks. Use fixed tick Δt=1/120s for normal logic (or 1/240 only if collision proof demands), with integer tick index and explicitly bounded control values. Serialize all source parameters as versioned codable data. No GPU or frame delta is authoritative for win/failure.
- **Player action:** Tune ground resonators to make dormant geometric plants unfold. Normalize input into `VibrationGardenAction` tagged with stable control ID, tick, local scene coordinates and deterministic quantization. Illegal actions return typed `ActionRejected(reason, visualCue)` without changing state.
- **Win predicate:** place emitters so returning wavefronts reveal an ordered signal pattern. For this particular product, all placed/checkpoint states must be satisfied concurrently and held for 6 fixed ticks, with no forbidden geometry contact or resource deficit. No shader-level visual similarity check substitutes for this predicate.
- **Failure predicate:** budget overrun, impossible state certificate, invalid component collisions, exhausted moves/time if explicitly signaled in the UI. Failure never silently corrupts a save or consumes premium content. Pause, undo and retry are always supported.
- **Solver:** discrete emitter search with exact arrival-order and occlusion checks. It must output a machine-readable witness list of actions and resulting digest, prove a bounded path for every shipped level, and generate a contrasting invalid action for negative tests. Reject a level when no witness exists, multiple solutions violate an intentionally unique puzzle, or gesture targets are inaccessible.
- **Numeric risks:** misleading sound analogy, ring overdraw and strobe risk. Use safe clamp and finite checks, bounded loops, stable sorting of equal-key entities, seed-controlled randomness and approximate predication only where tolerance is exposed in metadata. A NaN, Inf, zero-timestep or unsolved rule must be a test failure.
#### 5.17.3. First session storyboard, user experience and precise input intent
- **00:00–00:15 — Orient:** Open on a precompiled real scene depicting radial substrate ripples trigger recursive metallic blooms; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals; name the goal in under 12 words; color-independent icon for target; default silence is okay.
- **00:15–00:35 — One safe action:** Show a single draggable pulse propagation graph handle; allow tap and hold, drag-release, and undo with immediate visual response. No camera action while dragging an object.
- **00:35–00:55 — Reveal the rule:** Expose a target with tune ground resonators to make dormant geometric plants unfold; demonstrate the solver witness at quarter speed on repeatable seed without requiring a movie asset.
- **00:55–01:15 — First independent attempt:** Ask the player to complete one two-action challenge. A wrong action gets a preview and undo rather than confusing penalty.
- **01:15–01:35 — Reward and transition:** Present win state tied to authoritative pulse propagation graph predicate; show actual new generated visual composition rather than a pre-rendered reward.
- **01:35–02:00 — Player control and trust:** Expose pause, reduce flashing/motion, camera reset and offline save state; restart resumes without an account.
**Touch:** Position/trigger resonators and infer hidden 3D structure. Use one-finger object direct manipulation and a two-finger camera orbit, never allow unintentional camera movement while a target is captured. Minimum control size 44×44pt unless a physical-size, accessibility-audited alternative is provided. Offer focus cycling, keyboard controls where supported, descriptive VoiceOver state and noncolor target symbols. Camera pitch clamp, depth picking and undo are part of the contract.
#### 5.17.4. Renderer architecture, shader paths and actual code-generated visual recipe
**Geometry:** expanding ring meshes, volumetric-look pulse shells and glowing distance bands. Create bounded indexed vertices from numeric state, shader variants determined at build time, stable draw order, backface choices, wireframe-like overlays where beneficial and a shared scene descriptor. The renderer consumes immutable snapshots and interpolates between previous and current tick; GPU floating-point differences never decide a puzzle result.
**Visual signature:** radial substrate ripples trigger recursive metallic blooms; Instanced line meshes, transient wave shells, acoustically inspired distance-field reveals. To make this screenshot-worthy without asset artists: use curvature-based normals, a 3- or 4-stop analytical palette, thin edge emissive lighting, controlled depth-layer fog, instanced particle sparks, soft bloom in GLES3-safe framebuffer passes, and direct camera compositions. All texture-like detail comes from algebraic noise, ray-space gradients, distance-field contours or generated normals. Baked raster hero art is prohibited.
**GLES3 pipeline:** shared EGL surface & context from VisualCore; depth prepass or regular depth setup, opaque generated geometry, carefully sorted translucent geometry or weighted approximation only if available, emissive overlay, bounded separable blur, final color-management and UI composition. Rebuild resources after EGL context loss from CPU scene descriptor, not by reusing stale GL object handles. Establish 1×/2× adaptive sample budget after device evidence. Avoid unverified GLES extensions and always compile actual shader variants on both simulator toolchains.
**Numeric shader interface:** program ID `VibrationGardenScene`, `uTime` from fixed ticks, `uSeed` packed in stable integer uniforms, `uCamera`, `uQuality`, `uReduceMotion`, `uPaletteMode`, `VibrationGardenParams` uniform buffer equivalent compatible with audited ANGLE APIs. Validate all shader input domains and branch/loop bounds. Visual replay golden uses seed `23baae96db6d` and camera manifest, generated on actual renderer.
#### 5.17.5. Content production, balancing, progression and rewards
- **World 01, levels 001–010:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `1`, cap solver depth at 14 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤145 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 02, levels 011–020:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `2`, cap solver depth at 18 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤160 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 03, levels 021–030:** introduce at most 1 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `3`, cap solver depth at 22 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤175 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 04, levels 031–040:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `4`, cap solver depth at 26 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤190 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 05, levels 041–050:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `5`, cap solver depth at 30 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤205 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 06, levels 051–060:** introduce at most 2 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `6`, cap solver depth at 34 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤220 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 07, levels 061–070:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `7`, cap solver depth at 38 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤235 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 08, levels 071–080:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `8`, cap solver depth at 42 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤250 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 09, levels 081–090:** introduce at most 3 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `9`, cap solver depth at 46 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤265 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
- **World 10, levels 091–100:** introduce at most 4 distinct pulse propagation graph controls, quantize parameter complexity tier `10`, cap solver depth at 50 moves, guarantee at least one witness with normalized gesture travel ≤280 screen points at reference scale, seed ambient visual variation independently from the truth state, supply one zero-penalty redo tutorial for each introduced rule.
Every generated level has explicit human-readable objective, difficulty, result predicate, move/action budget, certified solver replay, rejected-action certificate, loadable scene, display camera, accessibility annotations, visual-quality tiers, content checksum and stable persistent identifier. Generate the catalog offline during build, include compressed indexed payloads if needed, and ship no huge generated sources in Git. Prevent repeats by comparing canonical normalized puzzle hashes, not simply seed numbers. A title cannot ship with 100 colorful screens that lack gameplay or unique solutions.
